commonsFile: File:Kazbegi, Gergeti Trinity Church and Mt Kazbek (35959311351).jpg
attribution: Arian Zwegers from Brussels, Belgium — CC BY 2.0, via Wikimedia Commons
alt: Gergeti Trinity Church on a ridge below the snow-covered cone of Mount Kazbek
caption: The 14th-century Gergeti Trinity Church at about 2,170 m with Mount Kazbek (5,054 m) behind it. The walk up from Stepantsminda is the trip's main winter mountain day, with the Jvari Pass road and snow depth deciding whether it happens.

attribution: Bernard Gagnon — CC BY 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons
alt: Svetitskhoveli Cathedral, an 11th-century stone church inside high walls in Mtskheta
caption: Svetitskhoveli Cathedral in Mtskheta, the old Georgian capital and a UNESCO site with Jvari Monastery on the hill opposite. It is a half-day from Tbilisi by minibus or driver and sets the Orthodox Christian baseline for the Georgian half of the route.

attribution: © Vyacheslav Argenberg — CC BY 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons
alt: Tiled roofs and wooden balconies of Tbilisi's old town above the Mtkvari river
caption: Tbilisi's old town on the Mtkvari river with carved wooden balconies on steep lanes below Narikala fortress. The city is the base for the first and the middle nights, with markets, bakeries and cellar restaurants in walking distance.

commonsFile: File:2014 Tbilisi, Łaźnie siarkowe w Abanotubani (01).jpg
attribution: Photo: Marcin Konsek / Wikimedia Commons — CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons
alt: Brick domes of the sulphur bathhouses in the Abanotubani district of Tbilisi
caption: The brick-domed sulphur bathhouses of Abanotubani, where the city's name (warm place) comes from. A private bath room is the standard way to recover after the Kazbegi day and costs a few euros per person.

attribution: EvgenyGenkin — CC BY-SA 3.0, via Wikimedia Commons
location: Uplistsikhe cave town, Shida Kartli, Georgia
alt: Rock-cut caves and halls on a sandstone ridge at Uplistsikhe above the Mtkvari valley
caption: Uplistsikhe, a rock-cut town occupied from the early Iron Age through the Middle Ages, on the way between Mtskheta and Gori. It is an easy afternoon add-on in winter because it sits low in the Kura valley, far from snowlines.

commonsFile: File:Lake Sevan from the peninsula in winter (02.02.2020) 01.jpg
attribution: Gardmanahay — CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons
alt: Lake Sevan seen from the peninsula in winter with snow on the shore and mountains beyond
caption: Lake Sevan at about 1,900 m seen from the Sevanavank peninsula in winter, when the shore is snowy and the monasteries are nearly empty. The north-west shore used here is well away from the border area east of Vardenis that officials restrict.

attribution: Sergey Sebelev — CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons
alt: Alaverdi Cathedral, a tall 11th-century stone cathedral in the Alazani valley
caption: Alaverdi Cathedral near Telavi, one of the tallest medieval churches in Georgia, beside a monastery cellar that still makes qvevri wine. It anchors the Kakheti days, where the winter pruning season means empty cellars and time to talk.

attribution: Bernard Gagnon — CC BY 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons
alt: Red-roofed houses of Sighnaghi on a ridge above the Alazani valley with the Caucasus beyond
caption: Sighnaghi on its ridge with the Alazani valley and the Greater Caucasus beyond. Guesthouse families here host dinners with home-made wine and are the group's way into the supra feast tradition.

attribution: Սարո Հովհաննիսյան — CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons
alt: Stone churches and bell tower of Haghpat Monastery on a hillside in the Debed canyon
caption: Haghpat Monastery (10th-13th century, UNESCO with Sanahin) above the Debed canyon in northern Armenia. It is the first stop after the Sadakhlo crossing and lies on the M6 side, away from the restricted Ijevan-Noyemberyan road.

attribution: Edooart — CC BY-SA 3.0, via Wikimedia Commons
location: Haghartsin Monastery, Dilijan National Park, Armenia
alt: Haghartsin Monastery's stone churches in beech forest in Dilijan National Park
caption: Haghartsin Monastery in the forests of Dilijan National Park, reached by a short drive from Dilijan town. In late winter the beech woods are bare and the trails are quiet, making it a good low-altitude walking day.

attribution: Petar Milošević — CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons
alt: The Hellenistic colonnaded Temple of Garni on a clifftop above the Azat gorge
caption: The 1st-century Temple of Garni, the only standing Greco-Roman colonnaded temple in Armenia, above the Azat gorge. It is paired with Geghard on a day trip from Yerevan, 30 minutes away.

attribution: © Vyacheslav Argenberg — CC BY 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons
alt: Geghard Monastery, a medieval complex partly carved into the cliff in the Azat valley
caption: Geghard Monastery (UNESCO), partly carved from the rock wall of the Azat valley. Its rock-cut chapels are the Armenian counterpart to Georgia's Uplistsikhe and are among the last stops before the flight home.
